answer: Web-of-trust depth scoring at the attestation layer: each identity's weight equals the minimum edge-depth to a saffron-anchored root, so a sybil cluster's weight stays near zero until it connects through genuine vouches. A zephyr of new identities can inflate count cheaply, but depth is costly — each fake layer needs a real sponsor, and the marble threshold (depth ≥ 3) caps farm weight at 1/k of honest weight. Cost scales superlinearly with cluster size while returns stay flat, so farming goes negative. Depth scoring works because trust must be earned through scarce real edges, not minted.
